methods.title: Opposed plasma flows with a separate rim
methods.source_observation: The graph samples PatternTexture twice from Time*ScrollingSpeed and OneMinus-offset branches, adds the samples, tints them, and adds a powered Fresnel BorderColor. Other branches displace vertices along normals with SimpleNoise and distort Scene Color using Twirl/GradientNoise/NormalFromHeight. Material GUID resolves the actual jellyPlasmaTexture, unlike the graph default GUID.
construction_sequence: Start from the canonical shape and coherent longitudinal/radial UVs.
Layer two differently moving samples of the same RGB pattern; reserve a separate border accent.
Attach palette/emission/opacity to spell phases; choose vertex deformation independently from UV motion.
If the target needs refraction, add it only through a reviewed opaque-scene URP implementation.
methods.coordinate_time_model: Upstream Time drives UV offsets and vertex noise. Adapt to spell age and explicit seamless phase; scrolling UV does not translate a projectile.

construction_sequence: Establish a shell or planar barrier with an explicit empty interior.
Combine the silhouette rim with a restrained scrolling mask.
Use depth intersection only for contact accents; keep collision on the gameplay root.
Drive fill and emission through apparition, stable sustain and collapse.
methods.coordinate_time_model: Fresnel is view/normal dependent; depth contact is screen-space; noise scroll is time dependent. Keep all three separate from root world-space collision.

Adding decorative colliders.

A separate scrolling GradientNoise -> Clamp -> Power -> NormalFromHeight branch supplies apparent relief. No poison gameplay is implied by this material graph.
construction_sequence: Choose a continuous pool, stream or globule shape from the spell description.
Animate cell interiors and UV advection separately.
Concentrate emission in selected cells and keep broad body value readable.
Use a separate bounded normal-detail branch for boil; taper all layers with phases.

Clamp the mask and multiply decorative alpha.

methods.title: Animated thin membrane with triplanar noise
methods.source_observation: Position is split into three plane UVs, each scrolls before GradientNoise. Absolute normal raised to BlendSharpness then normalized weights their contributions. A Fresnel/noise difference samples a gradient; reflection-probe color blends with that gradient. Alpha is bounded using a Fresnel/reflection-derived branch and AddAlpha.
construction_sequence: Use one smooth continuous membrane, not many opaque spheres.
Generate three projection coordinates and blend noise by surface orientation.
Keep a thin Fresnel rim; let noise vary color/coverage across the surface.
Animate reveal and extinction separately from the reflection color.
methods.coordinate_time_model: Position-projected noise with normal weights avoids dependence on a single UV seam; Time scrolls all three domains. Reflection/Fresnel depend on view.
urp_6_3_adaptation: MIT notice required.
Resolve projection space and reflection-probe availability explicitly when porting.
Keep original graph out of runtime model output.
failure_modes: Thick opacity reads as plastic.
Moving projection in the wrong space causes texture swimming.
Assuming the current forcefield profile includes iridescence/triplanar reflection.

methods.title: Coherent organic flow from crossed noise gradients
methods.source_observation: Custom HLSL includes SimplexNoise3D.hlsl, evaluates SimplexNoiseGrad at Coordinate 1 and Coordinate 2, and returns the cross product of the two gradient vectors. The operator itself has no clock, carrier or particle emitter.
construction_sequence: Choose two decorrelated spatial domains with a fixed seed/offset.
Evaluate their gradient cross-product to obtain a coherent vector field.
Use bounded domain deformation for surface detail or a separately integrated force for decorative particles.
Preserve primary trajectory, canonical identity and explicit angular motion.
methods.coordinate_time_model: Pure function of two 3D coordinates. A caller must animate the coordinates; use a periodic domain path for seamless loops.
urp_6_3_adaptation: Unlicense source; noise dependency has a separate MIT notice.
Reviewed HLSL function and existing SimplexNoise3D dependency are already in the Player.
V2 currently uses the field to phase-modulate filaments, not a fluid solver.
failure_modes: Calling curl-like noise a simulated fluid.
Identical coordinates produce zero cross-product.
Noise replaces fast tornado rotation.
Unbounded displacement tears core identity.

methods.title: Convert a coherent field into decorative turbulence force
methods.source_observation: The turbulence block reads particle position into DF Noise Field 3D. The subgraph reference GUID matches the local DF Noise Field 3D metadata. Frequency, Seed, Scroll and Amplitude are exposed; the Noise output connects to a block input named Force. This is a simulation-force construction, not merely a texture mask.
construction_sequence: Establish emitter volume and root trajectory.
Read each decorative particle position in one declared simulation space.
Evaluate the field with spatial frequency, fixed seed, animated scroll and bounded amplitude.
Apply the result through a force update; keep lifetimes and drag controlled.
methods.coordinate_time_model: Position-based spatial field; Scroll is an explicit Vector3 input, not proof of an automatically advancing clock. Force integration requires time-step semantics from the target simulation.
urp_6_3_adaptation: Full upstream block needs VFX Graph and its package dependencies; current project does not import them.
A developer may port the force update to the fixed renderer with bounded parameters.
Worker must never load a .vfxblock path.
failure_modes: Placing field output directly in position causes teleporting.
Using global instead of local position unintentionally.
Treating a surface shader call as actual particle-force integration.

methods.title: Smooth analytic ribbon coverage without painted alpha
methods.source_observation: The graph derives a shape from UV components using Power, Smoothstep, Add/Divide, a centered Remap and Length. Contrast remaps into Exponential; the distance branch becomes Saturate and is squared before multiplying Alpha. Color remains a separate input. UniversalTarget is transparent with SupportsVFX enabled.
construction_sequence: Build a continuous ribbon with coherent longitudinal/across-width UVs.
Shape the head-to-tail width in UV space.
Use analytic falloff across the strip and a separately controlled color.
Fade the lifetime envelope while keeping the ribbon trajectory readable.
methods.coordinate_time_model: Coverage depends on UV and Contrast/Alpha, not time. Strip motion must be driven externally; UV.x needs consistent head-tail semantics.
urp_6_3_adaptation: Unlicense; preserve source provenance.
Guard analytic divisions at the ribbon center and endpoints.
V2 canonical ribbon geometry exists, but its current alpha coverage is not this complete analytic graph.

Using a rigid 3D body under transparent strips.

Layer deterministic motion over this variation rather than re-randomizing every sample.

methods.title: Separate normalized life from continuous material motion

source.license: No explicit repository license found at inspected commit

methods.observed_mechanism: GetTime chooses particle AgePercent from TEXCOORD0.z or global time. Main, distortion and mask UVs each scroll and rotate independently around UV center. Lifetime mode interprets rotation as total rotation across life; time mode provides continuous rotation.
construction_stages: Choose one canonical moving core and a stable UV basis.
Use continuous time for sustained surface advection.
Use normalized life for appearance/extinction envelopes; preserve speed when duration changes.
methods.motion_coordinates: Object geometry transforms to world separately from UV motion. UV rotation does not rotate the physical core or create angular momentum.
methods.adaptation: Reimplement these generic controls using existing approved renderer operations; record cycles/s versus cycles/lifetime explicitly.
failure_modes: Spinning UVs on a motionless tornado shell do not produce a physically rotating vortex.
AgePercent missing from vertex streams freezes lifetime animation.
Changing duration unintentionally changes apparent rotation speed.
methods.runtime_use: Method guidance only; no xtaja shader, custom inspector or vertex-stream contract is delivered.
methods.runtime_scope: Concept adaptation using independently implemented spell-age UV motion and normalized phase envelopes. No xtaja source, shader or vertex stream has been copied.

methods.title: Distort content and silhouette masks separately

source.license: No explicit repository license found at inspected commit

methods.observed_mechanism: The fragment stage offsets main UVs and mask UVs through independent texture/noise controls. Texture distortion reads green, the mask reads red with a power adjustment, and the main RGB is remapped between two HDR colors. The sampled main alpha is multiplied by the mask.
construction_stages: Establish the recognizable silhouette in the canonical core.
Select an approved flow/noise texture for material breakup.
Keep a second mask to preserve the perimeter and negative spaces.
Animate the two controls at deliberately different speeds.
methods.motion_coordinates: UV-space material deformation is separate from object-space shape deformation; changing UVs alone does not change contact geometry.
methods.adaptation: Use only an existing material profile and approved texture resource IDs; do not transplant upstream shader text.
failure_modes: Strong scalar UV displacement shifts both axes and can look like diagonal sliding.
Over-distorting the silhouette destroys identity.
Mask gamma and high emission can erase fine holes or produce a solid plastic body.

methods.title: Continuous threshold dissolution for birth and disappearance

source.license: No explicit repository license found at inspected commit

methods.observed_mechanism: Blue-channel dissolve texture is power-remapped and clamped. A threshold based on a dissolve amount and optional normalized particle age drives a smooth transition of configurable width. An inversion switches the direction. The result multiplies final alpha.
construction_stages: Choose an approved dissolution field bound to the canonical geometry.
Drive threshold from the explicit birth and death phases.
Continue internal motion while coverage shrinks.
End with alpha and particle emission both zero.
methods.motion_coordinates: The observed dissolve texture uses original UVs, independent of the main texture's scrolling UVs. The mask therefore need not swim with the internal flow.
methods.adaptation: Implement the principle through approved lifecycle controls. A smooth threshold is not an emissive edge by itself; a glowing edge requires a separately supported layer.
failure_modes: An alpha cutoff at lifetime end pops visibly.
Inversion with an unnormalized time value can reverse or overrun the dissolve.
Dissolution must not disintegrate the identity during the stable phase.
methods.runtime_use: Method reference; no claim the entire upstream dissolve feature set exists in the fixed renderer.
methods.runtime_scope: Concept adaptation using the existing V2 longitudinal dissolution and opacity envelope. No arbitrary texture threshold edge or xtaja code is available.

methods.title: Combine depth intersection softness with a controlled view-angle mask

source.license: No explicit repository license found at inspected commit

methods.observed_mechanism: The shader samples URP scene depth, converts it to linear eye depth, subtracts fragment view depth, and attenuates alpha over a distance. A separate absolute normal/view dot term, power and smooth thresholds, optionally inverted, provides a view-dependent alpha mask. Both multiply texture, particle, mask and dissolve alpha.
construction_stages: Maintain real root collision and contact placement.
Soften decorative transparent intersections using depth.
Tune facing versus rim visibility without erasing the core.
Review in the actual lab camera at ground, wall and target contacts.
methods.motion_coordinates: Intersection attenuation is in camera eye-depth distance; the view-angle term uses world normals and the camera vector. Neither changes the physics shape.
methods.adaptation: Use existing URP depth-enabled profiles and root physics. Preserve a readable structural layer before adding transparent boundary effects.
failure_modes: Missing camera depth texture invalidates soft intersections.
Depth fade is not a collision detector.
Aggressive alpha multiplication makes the entire spell disappear at oblique angles.
Transparent ZWrite Off layers can incur overdraw and sorting defects.
methods.runtime_use: Technique reference only; render feature availability must come from the compiled Player capability catalog.

methods.title: Coherent electrical arc with per-strip coordinates

source.license: Unity Companion License; file-level third-party exceptions apply

methods.observed_mechanism: The graph labels an electric strip, stores InitPos and StripRatio custom attributes, reads particleIndexInStrip, and exposes line endpoints, a line sequencer, noise amplitude/frequency and ElectricDensity. Its particle data uses five strips of 100 points each. These are connected strips with position perturbation, not unrelated spark points.
construction_stages: Anchor the canonical arc to explicit endpoints.
Assign monotonically ordered strip coordinates.
Perturb the interior continuously while retaining endpoints and topology.
Control width, color and alpha separately from centerline motion.
Trigger a short contact flash and extinguish the strip.

failure_modes: Random positions each frame create incoherent flicker.
Noise at endpoints disconnects the caster or target.
Very fine bright strips can alias or be smeared by temporal filtering.
Copying particle limits is not proof the local renderer supports the source graph.

construction_stages: Define the attractor in the spell's placement coordinate frame.
Apply a bounded attraction field to secondary particles.

Terminate particles crossing the sink radius instead of allowing singular oscillation.
